outcome: A spell can be cast only if the mana spent matches the colored and colorless symbols and covers the generic part of its mana cost.
An object with no mana cost cannot be cast by paying its mana cost, so it is not castable unless an effect lets it be cast without paying.
An object's colors are the colors of the mana symbols in its mana cost.
An object whose mana cost has no colored symbols is colorless.
An object with two or more colors of symbols in its mana cost is each of those colors.
Hybrid and Phyrexian symbols in a mana cost make the object all of those symbols' colors.
An object with a color indicator is each color the indicator denotes.
An effect that changes color, adds a color or removes all color changes the object's colors.
An object's mana value equals the total mana in its mana cost, which decides what mana-value-conditioned effects do.
An object with no mana cost has mana value 0, except a nonmodal double-faced back face or melded permanent.
A nonmodal double-faced back face has its front face's mana value, and a copy of it has mana value 0.
A melded permanent has the combined mana value of its front faces, and a copy of it has mana value 0.
A split card off the stack has the combined mana value of its halves; on the stack it has that of the chosen half.
X counts as 0 in mana value off the stack and as the chosen value on the stack.
A hybrid symbol contributes its largest component to mana value.
Each Phyrexian mana symbol contributes 1 to mana value.
